slides.title: Cultivating T|+⟩, S|+⟩ and Z|+⟩ states
slides.caption: Unitary injection and d=3 cultivation under uniform depolarizing noise p (labels). The paper ran a state-vector simulation of every gate; Tsim samples the same circuits.

slides.title: Injection and cultivation without escape
slides.caption: Three injection styles with d=3 cultivation, and unitary injection with d=5, at p = 0.05%, 0.1% and 0.2%. The paper sampled the S-gate stand-in with Stim, up to 10¹² shots per point; Tsim samples the stand-in and the real T gates.
notes: The paper saw no error in 10¹² shots at d=5, p=0.05%: its point is an upper bound (open marker).

slides.title: Cultivation on RP² vs. the colour code
slides.caption: Ungrown cultivation at p = 0.1%: logical error rate per kept shot (± one standard deviation) and the fraction of shots kept. The paper sampled the S-gate stand-in with Stim; Tsim samples the stand-in and the real T gates.
notes: The paper gives no uncertainties; its values are compared as rounded to the printed digits.

slides.title: Cultivation with Clifford measurements by gauging
slides.caption: Logical error rate per kept shot (± one standard deviation) and success rate at final distance 3 and 5. The paper sampled the |+i⟩ stand-in with Stim; Tsim samples the stand-in and the real T state.
notes: The authors' generator at its released commit keeps 68% of the shots at d=3, p=0.05%, against the 65% printed in the paper; the error rates agree. The paper prints success rates to two digits without uncertainties.

slides.title: Gauging cultivation, d=3: stand-in and T state
slides.caption: Logical error rate against the success probability for p = 0.1% to 0.5% (labels). The paper sampled the |+i⟩ stand-in with Stim and Qiskit, and the T state with Qiskit's state-vector simulator; Tsim samples both.
notes: The paper's Qiskit |T⟩ point at p=0.1% rests on a single logical error, hence its wide interval.

slides.title: Cultivation on the unrotated surface code
slides.caption: H-state cultivation, logical error rate against expected attempts for p = 0.02% to 0.8% (labels): the paper's Clifford approximation and the circuit with real T gates.

paper.label: Paper (state vector)
paper.quoted: about 10⁶ CPU hours, about 10⁷ shots per point

notes: The paper's full state-vector points are shown only as a figure, so only Tsim's data is plotted.

slides.title: Cultivation's degraded fault distance, d=3
slides.caption: Logical error rate before escape against the noise strength, for the original double check and with the paper's Z flags. With real T gates the original circuit loses a power of p; the flags restore it.
notes: The paper released no numbers for this figure, so only Tsim's data is plotted.

slides.title: Z flags at d=5, with real T gates
slides.caption: Logical error rate before escape against expected attempts, for p = 0.05% to 0.3% (labels). The flags cut the error rate 5 to 11 times at almost no cost in kept shots.
notes: The paper released no numbers for this figure, so only Tsim's data is plotted.

slides.title: Fold-transversal cultivation: |Y⟩ vs. |H_XY⟩
slides.caption: Fault-distance-3 cultivation without escape, logical error rate against expected attempts for p = 0.05% to 0.7% (labels).
notes: The paper released no numbers for this panel, so only Tsim's data is plotted.

Read off the paper's figure, its |Y⟩ point at p=0.1% is about 1.8 × 10⁻⁷, against 5 × 10⁻⁸ here: the paper's circuit for this panel has more fault locations than the one its released generator produces.

slides.title: Hook injection with erasure qubits
slides.caption: Logical error rate against acceptance for hook injection at d=3: without erasures at p = 0.1%, and with erasure qubits (erasure rate e, residual p = 0.01%), where shots with a detected erasure are discarded. The paper sampled the S stand-in.
notes: Tsim samples the hook circuit released with the paper. Its noise model differs from the circuits behind the released data, which explains the higher error rate (about 2×) without erasures.

slides.title: Small-angle injection with STAR
slides.caption: Postselected logical error rate of transversal small-angle rotations, against the noise strength, at a logical angle of 0.01 rad, for d = 3, 5 and 7.
notes: Tsim samples QuEra's public STAR challenge circuits under uniform depolarizing noise, not the paper's hardware-aware noise model, so the curves are not expected to coincide with the paper's, which released no numbers.

slides.title: Small-angle injection with STAR
slides.caption: Postselected logical error rate of transversal small-angle rotations, against the rotation angle, at p = 0.073%, for d = 3, 5 and 7.
notes: Tsim samples QuEra's public STAR challenge circuits under uniform depolarizing noise, not the paper's hardware-aware noise model, so the curves are not expected to coincide with the paper's, which released no numbers.

slides.title: Logical tomography of the injected state
slides.caption: Postselected logical ⟨X⟩ and ⟨Z⟩ for 24 injected angles θ, SI1000 noise at p = 0.3%: injection alone, and with d=3 cultivation, which projects every input onto the magic axis (dotted). Star: the ideal T state.
notes: The paper's grey simulation points are not released, so only Tsim's data is plotted.

slides.title: Kickback tomography against the injected angle
slides.caption: Logical error of the whole kickback-tomography circuit against the injected angle θ, SI1000 noise at p = 0.23%. Cultivation with QEC cycles is lowest at θ = π/4, the T state (dotted).
notes: The paper's grey simulation points are not released, so only Tsim's data is plotted.

slides.title: Tomography after grafting to the surface code
slides.caption: Logical ⟨X⟩ and ⟨Z⟩ after growing the cultivated state into a d=5 surface code and idling N QEC cycles, SI1000 noise at p = 0.23%. Star: the ideal T state.
notes: The paper decodes the grafted surface code with a decoder; here every detector is postselected, so these points are a decoder-free upper bound on the fidelity, not the paper's protocol.
The paper's grey simulation points are not released, so only Tsim's data is plotted.
